findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 30% to 70% in embedded post author link
findings.body: The `.topic-meta-data h5 a` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR rewrote it as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is now 70% instead of 30%. This contradicts the PR's goal of only adding a dark-theme branch. Light themes will render embedded post author names much lighter and with less contrast than before. The pattern used elsewhere in the PR would give `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% for custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule uses 30% for the light branch and $secondary at 70% for the dark branch, which inverts the intended mapping. On light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before. The expected rewrite is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Topic map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The PR changed it to 50% (with a 50% $secondary dark branch), which alters the light-theme appearance. The desktop counterpart correctly uses 20%/80%, so the mobile rule is now inconsistent with desktop and with its own previous value.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now 50%/50%. That unintentionally lightens member names on light themes. The pattern used elsewhere in the PR would give `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The same regression appears in mobile/user.scss line 497.
